_note.what: Half-year (interim) results, typed by hand from the company's own results announcement. Yahoo publishes NOTHING sub-annual for semi-annual reporters — not on the local line, not on the OTC ADR, not in any quoteSummary module — so without this file those names sit on a figure up to twelve months old.
_note.who: Companies that report twice a year rather than four times: the HK Main Board issuers (HKEx requires interim + annual, not quarterly) plus M&S. Run `npm run interim` for the current list and what is missing — it is derived from the store, never a hardcoded list, so a name drops off by itself once quarters appear for it. Nintendo and the French names were on this list until quoteSummary started supplying their quarters; absence of quarterly data in one Yahoo endpoint is NOT evidence a company reports semi-annually, which is why the list is worth re-reading rather than trusting from memory.
_note.shape: One array per Yahoo symbol, oldest first. Amounts are in the company's REPORTING currency, as filed, in full units (not millions) — the same convention as earnings.json, which is what the page compares them against.

fields.end: Period end, YYYY-MM-DD (the H1 balance date, e.g. 2026-06-30).
fields.published: Date the results were announced, YYYY-MM-DD.
fields.source: Direct https link to the announcement or results PDF.
fields.currency: Reporting currency; must match this ticker's currency in earnings.json.
fields.opinc: Operating income for the six months (omit if the company does not report one).
fields.nic: Net income attributable to shareholders for the six months.
fields.eps: Basic or diluted EPS for the six months, per share, in the reporting currency.

_note.rule: Never estimate a missing figure. Omit the field, or omit the period. A blank cell is a fact; an invented one is not. `npm run interim` refuses entries whose revenue exceeds the filed full year, which is what a units slip (millions typed as units) looks like.
